answer: How can agents in a haven vote without being inundated by Sybils in the meadow? Each agent must prove they lie on a unique vertex of a shared knowledge graph. A Sybil attacker must forge an entirely distinct graph neighborhood, burning scarce human time to fabricate plausible edges. Since each vertex proof requires manual curation, parallel farming is impossible. The cost? Linear review time per fake identity, with no bulk-discount from volume.
